dec-25.quote: Our Saviour, dearly-beloved, was born today: let us be glad. For there is no proper place for sadness, when we keep the birthday of the Life, which destroys the fear of mortality and brings to us the joy of promised eternity.
dec-25.who: St. Leo the Great, Sermon on the Nativity
dec-25.question: Where in your day will you let joy, not worry, have the last word, because the Saviour has been born for you?

dec-26.quote: By the death of martyrs religion has been defended, faith increased, the Church strengthened; the dead have conquered, the persecutors have been overcome.
dec-26.who: St. Ambrose, On the Belief in the Resurrection
dec-26.question: Stephen forgave the very people stoning him. Whose wrong against you could you release today, praying for that person by name?

dec-27.quote: If, therefore, God gave to thee grace, because He gave freely, love freely. Do not for the sake of reward love God; let Him be the reward.
dec-27.question: God loved you first and freely. Whom can you love today with no expectation of return, simply because you were loved?

dec-28.quote: The Lord desired that we should rejoice and leap for joy in persecutions, because, when persecutions occur, then are given the crowns of faith, then the soldiers of God are proved, then the heavens are opened to martyrs.
dec-28.who: St. Cyprian, Letter to the People of Thibaris
dec-28.question: Rachel weeps while heaven opens to the little ones. For whom are you tempted to despair, and how could you entrust them to God today?

dec-29.quote: It is not necessary for being with God to be always at church; we may make an oratory of our heart, wherein to retire from time to time, to converse with Him in meekness, humility, and love.
dec-29.who: Brother Lawrence, The Practice of the Presence of God
dec-29.question: Simeon met Christ because he was led into the Temple. What small, quiet place in your day could become your own oratory of the heart?

dec-30.quote: He takes a body of our Nature, and that of a spotless Virgin, in whose womb He makes it His own, wherein to reveal Himself, conquer death, and restore life.
dec-30.who: St. Athanasius, On the Incarnation of the Word
dec-30.question: God took a body to give you life. What part of your ordinary, bodily life can you offer to Him today?

dec-31.quote: Thou awakest us to delight in Thy praise; for Thou madest us for Thyself, and our heart is restless, until it repose in Thee.
dec-31.question: Looking back over this year, what is one gift you can name aloud in praise before the year closes?

jan-02.quote: Therefore, to say, “they shall call” Him “Emmanuel,” means nothing else than that they shall see God amongst men.
jan-02.who: St. John Chrysostom, Homilies on Matthew
jan-02.question: Emmanuel means God is with us. Where this week do you need to notice His presence among people rather than seek Him elsewhere?

jan-03.quote: But because “the Word was made flesh, and dwelt among us,” by His very nativity he made an eye-salve to cleanse the eyes of our heart, and to enable us to see His majesty by means of His humility.
jan-03.question: The Word became flesh in humility. Which humble, ordinary thing in front of you can help clear your eyes to see His majesty?

jan-04.quote: And just as through a disobedient virgin man was stricken down and fell into death, so through the Virgin who was obedient to the Word of God man was reanimated and received life.
jan-04.who: St. Irenaeus, Demonstration of the Apostolic Preaching
jan-04.question: Mary pondered and obeyed. What word of God have you heard lately, and what one obedient step could you take on it today?

jan-05.quote: For the unwonted splendour of a bright new star appeared to the wise men and filled their mind with such wonder, as they gazed upon its brilliance, that they could not think they ought to neglect what was announced to them with such distinctness.
jan-05.who: St. Leo the Great, Sermon on the Epiphany
jan-05.question: The Magi followed a sign they could have ignored. What nudge toward God have you been neglecting that you could follow this week?

jan-06.quote: If those men journeyed so far to see Him newly born, what sort of excuse wilt thou have, not going out of thy way one alley’s length, that thou mayest visit Him sick or in bonds?
jan-06.who: St. John Chrysostom, Homilies on Matthew
jan-06.question: The Magi travelled far to worship. Whom could you visit this week, the sick or lonely, as a gift offered to Christ?

jan-07.quote: With the servants the Lord, with the criminals the Judge, cometh to be baptized. But be not thou troubled; for in these humiliations His exaltation doth most shine forth.
jan-07.who: St. John Chrysostom, Homilies on Matthew
jan-07.question: Jesus stood among sinners in humility. Where might you step down from being right or important and stand alongside someone today?

jan-08.quote: Wherefore were the heavens opened? To inform thee that at thy baptism also this is done, God calling thee to thy country on high, and persuading thee to have nothing to do with earth.
jan-08.who: St. John Chrysostom, Homilies on Matthew
jan-08.question: The heavens opened at Jesus’ baptism and at yours. What earthly attachment could you loosen today to hear the call to your heavenly home?

jan-09.quote: They heard that “He taketh away the sin of the world,” and straightway they ran to Him.
jan-09.who: St. John Chrysostom, Homilies on John
jan-09.question: Hearing that He takes away sin, people ran to Him. What sin or burden will you bring to Him in confession or prayer today?

jan-10.quote: The dove is that in the form of which the Holy Spirit descended, as you have read in the New Testament, Who inspires in you peace of soul and tranquillity of mind.
jan-10.question: The Spirit came as a gentle dove. Where could you answer a sharp word with peace and a calm mind today?

jan-11.quote: The mystery of this boon is great, dearly beloved, and this gift exceeds all gifts that God should call man son, and man should name God Father: for by these terms we perceive and learn the love which reached so great a height.
jan-11.who: St. Leo the Great, Sermon on the Nativity
jan-11.question: You are called a child of God. What would change in how you speak to Him this week if you prayed as a beloved son or daughter?

jan-12.quote: For He is the same God who, throughout the whole creation, worketh miracles every day, which become lightly esteemed by men, not because of the ease with which they are wrought, but by reason of their constant recurrence.
jan-12.question: We grow used to miracles that happen every day. What ordinary gift, such as food, health or friendship, will you receive today as a sign of His glory?

jan-13.quote: Jesus sanctified Baptism by being Himself baptized. If the Son of God was baptized, what godly man is he that despiseth Baptism?
jan-13.who: St. Cyril of Jerusalem, Catechetical Lectures
jan-13.question: Christ sanctified baptism by receiving it. How will you honour your own baptism today, perhaps with the sign of the cross and a prayer of thanks?

lent-1.quote: For darkened affections is removal from Thee. For it is not by our feet, or change of place, that men leave Thee, or return unto Thee.
lent-1.question: We return to God by turning our hearts, not moving our feet. What one inner habit will you turn from this Lent, and what will you turn toward?

lent-2.quote: As far as I can understand, the gate by which to enter this castle is prayer and meditation.
lent-2.who: St. Teresa of Avila, The Interior Castle
lent-2.question: Jesus says to go into your room and pray in secret. When and where will you keep a fixed quiet time with Him this week?

lent-3.quote: It therefore belongs to a virtuous life to show mercy and to fast in secret; that thou mayest seem to be seeking a reward from thy God alone, and not from men.
lent-3.who: St. Ambrose, On the Duties of the Clergy
lent-3.question: Fasting is joined to mercy and kept hidden. What will you give up quietly this week, and who will receive what you save?

lent-4.quote: Lend unto Him who wants nothing, yet hath need for thy sake; who feeds all men, yet is an hungered, that thou mayest not suffer famine; who is poor, that thou mayest be rich.
lent-4.who: St. John Chrysostom, Homilies on Matthew
lent-4.question: Christ is poor so that you may be rich. Whom will you help this week, trusting that you are lending to Him?

lent-5.quote: For who, that is set in the uncertainty of this life, can be found either exempt from temptation, or free from fault?
lent-5.who: St. Leo the Great, Sermon on Lent
lent-5.question: Even Jesus was tempted in the desert. Which temptation returns to you most often, and what is your plan for the moment it comes?

lent-6.quote: It remains, therefore, that we should understand the daily bread as spiritual, that is to say, divine precepts, which we ought daily to meditate and to labour after.
lent-6.who: St. Augustine, Our Lord’s Sermon on the Mount
lent-6.question: Man lives by every word from God. What passage of Scripture will you read and keep with you each day this week?

lent-7.quote: For as soon as He had said to him, “Get thee hence,” He caused him to take to flight; since he brought not against Him any other temptations.
lent-7.who: St. John Chrysostom, Homilies on Matthew
lent-7.question: Jesus answered the tempter with a single firm word and the tempter left. What short, firm answer will you give when your own temptation comes?

lent-8.quote: And in this Transfiguration the foremost object was to remove the offence of the cross from the disciple’s heart, and to prevent their faith being disturbed by the humiliation of His voluntary Passion by revealing to them the excellence of His hidden dignity.
lent-8.who: St. Leo the Great, Homily on the Transfiguration
lent-8.question: Jesus showed His glory to prepare His friends for the cross. What hard thing ahead can you face by recalling a moment God has shown Himself to you?

lent-9.quote: And what saith the voice? “This is my beloved Son.” Now if He is beloved, fear not thou, O Peter.
lent-9.who: St. John Chrysostom, Homilies on Matthew
lent-9.question: The Father says, “Listen to him.” What command of Jesus have you been avoiding, and what small step will you take on it today?

lent-10.quote: But what other counsel is there than this, that he who desires to have divine help for his own infirmity should bear that of others, and should assist it as much as possible?
lent-10.who: St. Augustine, Our Lord’s Sermon on the Mount
lent-10.question: We receive God’s mercy as we bear with others’ weakness. Whose faults will you carry patiently today instead of correcting or avoiding them?

lent-11.quote: For in no other sentence do we pray in such a way that we, as it were, enter into a compact with God: for we say, “Forgive us, as we also forgive.” And if we lie in that compact, the whole prayer is fruitless.
lent-11.who: St. Augustine, Our Lord’s Sermon on the Mount
lent-11.question: Every time you pray the Our Father, you make a promise to forgive. Whom do you need to forgive, and what will you do about it this week?

lent-12.quote: Let us remit, that we may have remission: let us grant the pardon which we crave: let us not be eager to be revenged when we pray to be forgiven.
lent-12.who: St. Leo the Great, Sermon on Lent
lent-12.question: Peter asked how often to forgive. Which old grievance will you set down this week, rather than saving it to bring up again?

lent-13.quote: Nothing else, however elevated, perfects the soul which must never seek to forget its own nothingness. Let humility be always at work, like the bee at the honeycomb, or all will be lost.
lent-13.who: St. Teresa of Avila, The Interior Castle
lent-13.question: The tax collector asked only for mercy and went home justified. Where can you stop defending yourself and simply tell God the truth about yourself?

lent-14.quote: That He may heal us, let us take His yoke upon us, and learn of Him who is meek and lowly in heart, and we shall find rest unto our souls: for His yoke is easy, and His burden is light.
lent-14.question: Jesus invites you to learn from Him, gentle and lowly. What burden of pride or worry could you set down in order to take up His yoke?

lent-15.quote: Because thou hast eyes to see the heavens: a heart thou hast not yet to see the Maker of heaven: therefore came He from heaven to earth, to cleanse the heart, that He may be seen who made heaven and earth.
lent-15.who: St. Augustine, Expositions on the Psalms
lent-15.question: Only a clean heart can see God, and He heals patiently. What wound will you let Him treat, even if it is uncomfortable?

lent-16.quote: For it is not so much the corruptible flesh as the clean heart, which is made a shrine for God, and a temple of the Holy Ghost.
lent-16.question: God makes His dwelling in a clean heart, not in outward show. What one thing needs cleaning out of your heart before Easter?
